newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut gains Thai life insurance licence.
newsitem.headline: NatMut gains Thai life insurance licence.

text.p: Australian insurance group National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had been granted a licence to operate in Thailand with two Thai partners.
"Thailand has now opened up with the granting of this and other licences," managing director Geoff Tomlinson said in a statement.

National Mutual, owned 51 percent by recently expanded French insurance giant Axa SA, said it and Thailand's second largest commercial bank, Krung Thai Bank would hold 45 percent each of the new venture.
Thai businessman Chinavais Sarasas will hold the balance.
National Mutual said it would manage the new company, to be called Krungthai AXA Life, operating a full-time agency force with Krung Thai also assisting product distribution.
"We are confident that this wide distribution network will provide us with a strong entry point into this market," Tomlinson said.
National Mutual said its total investment in Krungthai AXA Life was expected to be about A$11 million.
Tomlison said Thailand's long term economic outlook was positive despite a recent slowing in growth there.
"The potential for the Thai life insurance market is apparent when one considers life insurance penetration in only 10 percent in a population of more than 60 million," he said.
Thailand's life insurance market is currently serviced by 13 companies.
National Mutual, which aims to be a heavyweight in the Asian market, is awaiting China's approval of an operating licence. It also has plans to enter India, Vietnam and the Philippines.
